evidence: Cic. N.D. 1.66: corpuscula quaedam lēvia, alia aspera (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Smooth to the touch and to the eye, the opposite of asper. Not to be confused with levis, “light”, with a short e: Comenius sets the two side by side (below). Making something smooth is lēvigāre (see iron).

phrases.latin: illōs repertī in lītore calculī lēvēs et aliquid habentēs varietātis dēlectant
phrases.english: smooth pebbles found on the beach, with a bit of colour in them, delight them

phrases.latin: Manus dīgnōscit tangendō … calidum et frīgidum, ūmidum et siccum, dūrum et molle, lēve et asperum, grave et leve.
phrases.english: The hand tells by touch … hot and cold, wet and dry, hard and soft, smooth and rough, heavy and light.
